before.source_excerpt: The claim that zero collision entropy production for a symmetric elastic collision measure forces every positive integrable velocity density to be Maxwellian is false without a full-support assumption.

after.source_excerpt:
Let $v,w,v\prime,w\prime\in\mathbb R^3$ be velocities measured in metres per second, let $dv$ be three-dimensional Lebesgue measure, and set $Q_{m el}:=\{(v,w,v\prime,w\prime):v+w=v\prime+w\prime,\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v\prime|^2+|w\prime|^2\}$. Let $
u$ be a nonnegative countably additive measure on $Q_{m el}$ invariant under exchange of either velocity pair and interchange of incoming and outgoing pairs. For a positive finite-valued Lebesgue-measurable velocity density $g\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ whose four coordinate evaluations on $Q_{m el}$ are $
u$-measurable, set $A_g:=g(v)g(w)$ and $B_g:=g(v\prime)g(w\prime)$, and define the possibly infinite collision entropy production by $\mathscr P_
u(g):= rac14\int_{Q_{m el}}(A_g-B_g)\log(A_g/B_g)\,d
u$. A Maxwellian means a function $C\exp(-|v-U|^2/(2	heta))$ for a density scale $C>0$ with the units of $g$, a velocity $U\in\mathbb R^3$, and squared speed $	heta>0$. Full support means every nonempty relatively open subset of $Q_{m el}$ has positive $
u$-measure. The proposed implication that $\mathscr P_
u(g)=0$ forces $g$ to be Maxwellian for every such symmetric $
u$ and positive integrable $g$ is false without a full-support assumption on $
u$.
